access_model.quote: The Google Ads API has access levels associated with the Google Cloud project, and uses an application review process to grant various access levels.

access_notes.value: Enabling the Google Ads API in a Google Cloud project automatically grants Test access (test accounts only, 15,000 operations/day). Production account access requires an application review: Explorer (automated review in most cases, 2,880 operations/day against production), Basic (reviewed, 15,000/day), or Standard (review typically 10 business days, unlimited operations). The API itself is free at all access levels, but Standard-access apps are audited for Required Minimum Functionality and may incur non-compliance fees. A developer token is required in the developer-token header on every call, and the OAuth client must live in the same Cloud project as the API access level. The official MCP server is distributed as an open-source Python package with stdio or Cloud Run streamable-http transport; no hosted endpoint URL is published.
access_notes.quote: After you enable the Google Ads API (which grants Test access), you can immediately apply on the Google Ads API Overview page in the Google Cloud Console for Explorer access (automated review and approval in most cases, for up to 2,880 operations per day against production accounts).

official_mcp_server.quote: The Google Ads MCP server provides a standardized bridge to the Google Ads API.

rate_limits.value: Daily operation limits by access level: Test 15,000/day; Explorer 2,880/day against production and 15,000/day against test accounts; Basic 15,000/day; Standard unlimited. Max 10,000 mutate operations per request; Planning Service 1 QPS; Conversion Upload 2,000 conversions per request; gRPC response messages up to 64 MB.
rate_limits.quote: Mutate requests are limited to 10,000 operations per request, in addition to counting against the daily operation quota.

sandbox_or_test_env.quote: After you've enabled Google Ads API, your Google Cloud project is granted Test access.

api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.value: API is versioned by numeric releases (current reference is v26). Developer tokens were sunset on September 9, 2026, and API access levels are now managed per Google Cloud project.
api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.quote: Developer tokens were sunset on September 9, 2026, and API access levels are now managed per Google Cloud project.

verdict_reason: The Google Ads API is public, documented, free to use, and broad (campaigns, ads, reporting, billing across v26), with OAuth 2.0 plus a developer token and an instantly granted Test access level. However, production account access requires an application review process across Explorer/Basic/Standard levels, and Standard review can take 10 business days with Required Minimum Functionality audits. That review gate, not credentials sales, is what keeps it out of the easy tier.
main_blocker: Application review required for production access levels (Explorer/Basic/Standard)
open_questions: No fetched source lists official SDK languages; the client-libraries page appeared in the search index but its text was not included in the evidence bundle.
The official Google Ads MCP server has no published hosted endpoint URL; evidence documents stdio and Cloud Run streamable-http transports only, so the docs URL was used in its place.
Webhook capability is supported only by the developers.google.com/google-ads landing-page mention; the dedicated webhook overview/implementation pages were not included in the bundle.
Only the adwords OAuth scope is documented in the fetched auth pages; a full scope/permission list was not available in evidence.
The API versioning/sunset-dates policy page was not included in the fetched evidence, so the deprecation cadence beyond the developer-token sunset is unverified.
Whether Explorer access is always granted automatically or sometimes requires manual review is stated only as 'automated review and approval in most cases'.
